summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
## Summary

DDD-ADIV is the recommended design default for code projects using SocratexPipeline.

DDD-ADIV means Domain-Driven, Architecture-Decisive, Invariant-Visible development. The practical goal is an executable domain model: code should express real domain concepts, legal state transitions, ownership, and invariants directly, while framework/runtime adapters and lean performance representations remain secondary projections of that domain truth.

known_solutions_alignment.title: Known-Solutions Alignment
known_solutions_alignment.body:
## Known-Solutions Alignment

Use known solutions as domain-clarifying tools, not as abstract ceremony.

Before custom design:

- check known solutions, proven practices, standard tools, and business/software archetypes,
- compare the problem against architecture archetypes such as layered architecture, hexagonal architecture, CQRS, state machines, queues, adapters, repositories, and domain services,
- prefer build-vs-borrow discipline when a framework feature, library, workflow, or pattern is cheaper and clearer,
- check future fit before executing requested work, and recommend a better prerequisite or design when the requested route would create avoidable retrofit cost,
- align the selected solution with domain language, ownership, invariants, and boundaries.

Reject a known solution only when it conflicts with the domain, creates worse coupling, weakens invariants, or hides the source of truth.

domain_driven.title: Domain-Driven
domain_driven.body:
## Domain-Driven

Use project language as the primary naming source.

Prefer:

- business-meaningful names over mechanism names,
- explicit domain state over incidental data shape,
- commands and policies that describe intent,
- domain services only when behavior does not naturally belong to one entity or value object.

Avoid:

- generic managers that own unrelated behavior,
- anemic data objects plus scattered rules,
- framework vocabulary leaking into core domain logic,
- hidden domain meaning encoded only in comments or UI labels.

domain_model_executable_contract.title: Executable Domain Model
domain_model_executable_contract.body:
## Executable Domain Model

Treat the codebase as an executable model of the domain, not merely as implementation machinery.

Apply domain-driven, design-by-contract, type/schema-driven, rich-domain-model, and encapsulation principles where they make the system clearer and safer. Domain APIs, modules, types, records, schemas, states, and data contracts should use real domain concepts and terminology. State should change through explicit domain operations and legal transitions, not arbitrary external mutation. Make illegal states unrepresentable whenever practical; otherwise validate early at boundaries and protect invariants with runtime checks, assertions, tests, schemas, or other mechanisms available in the stack.

Prefer:

- `invoice.MarkPaid(payment)` over `invoice.Status = "paid"`,
- `CustomerId`, `InvoiceId`, `RouteId`, or `JobId` over interchangeable primitive identifiers,
- explicit transitions such as `Draft -> Submitted -> Approved -> Archived` over independent booleans that can contradict each other.

Use immutable value objects for values. Use mutable encapsulated entities for things with identity that evolve through time. Use pure functions when the domain naturally represents a transformation or calculation, but do not force functional programming or universal immutability onto entities whose domain meaning is persistent identity with controlled state change.

Keep framework, engine, database, transport, UI, and runtime concepts outside the domain core. Adapters translate external observations and commands into explicit domain contracts and translate domain results back out.

Performance and scale do not conflict with this rule. Hot-path, batch, storage, runtime, or high-volume code may use lean structures such as arrays, structs/records, tables, indexes, caches, buffers, projections, batch queries, generated views, or data-oriented layouts when the platform supports them. Treat those shapes as execution representations of the domain contract, not as a second hidden source of domain truth.

Do not introduce abstractions merely for architectural purity. Every abstraction should represent a real domain concept, enforce a useful contract, isolate an external dependency, or materially reduce future change cost. Do not turn every noun into a class, every class into an interface, or every state change into an elaborate pattern.

Code should be as simple as the domain allows, but not simpler than the domain.

architecture_decisive.title: Architecture-Decisive
architecture_decisive.body:
## Architecture-Decisive

Make durable ownership and dependency decisions explicit.

Prefer:

- small boundaries with clear responsibilities,
- ports and adapters for external systems,
- dependency direction that points inward toward stable domain logic,
- explicit source-of-truth ownership,
- decision records for choices that future work must preserve.

Avoid:

- circular ownership,
- duplicated sources of truth,
- convenience coupling across unrelated modules,
- broad shared utility layers that hide domain meaning.

invariant_visible.title: Invariant-Visible
invariant_visible.body:
## Invariant-Visible

Make important rules mechanically findable and checkable.

Prefer:

- validation at boundaries,
- explicit constructors or factories for valid states,
- assertions or guards for impossible states,
- schema checks for external data,
- tests for high-risk invariants,
- named policies for conditional rules.

Avoid:

- relying on call order when a state machine or explicit phase would be clearer,
- implicit defaults that silently create invalid states,
- scattered checks that implement one invariant differently in multiple places.

verification_attached.title: Verification-Attached
verification_attached.body:
## Verification-Attached

Attach verification to risky work.

Verification can be:

- unit tests,
- integration tests,
- contract tests,
- typechecks,
- linters,
- build checks,
- smoke tests,
- manual reproduction steps.

If verification is not practical, record the residual risk.
